page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by the AMD EPYC 9T34 processor running at a base clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provisions 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB, providing a standard compute-oriented ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware vector instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16 are fully enabled alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic extensions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance includes 20 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, contains no integrated local storage, and does not include GPU accelerators.

Performance benchmarks reflect strong per-core computational capabilities, with stress-ng single-core execution placing in the top ten percent and Geekbench single-core and multi-core evaluations falling within the top quartile. Cryptographic processing in PassMark also ranks in the top twenty-five percent, aided by hardware-accelerated instructions. Multi-threaded decompression and multi-core throughput operate near mid-tier baselines, achieving 182.7 GB/s in bzip3 tests and 49,846.52 points in multi-core stress-ng. Memory subsystems register 96.08 GB/s of large-block uncached read bandwidth and 56.28 GB/s write bandwidth.

Because the instance does not feature bundled local storage, persistent disk operations rely entirely on remote network-attached block storage. The compute-centric memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU establishes high CPU density per dollar for execution workloads, though it is unsuited for massive in-memory caching layers. The configuration is appropriate for compute-heavy batch processing, web serving clusters, cryptographic pipelines, Continuous Integration builds, and application backends requiring stable single-thread compute.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8ae.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9T34 processor clocked at 3.4 GHz. Featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores and 64.0 GB of system memory, it implements a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio suited for CPU-intensive tasks. The platform includes AVX-512 vector support, cryptographic extensions, and 20 Gbps baseline networking, without local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate strong single-thread efficiency and robust encryption handling, positioning the instance for distributed application services, microservices backends, continuous integration pipelines, and media transcoding.
